# Getting help

Atlas Todo is a spare-time project with one maintainer. Please pick the right place, so the
answer helps the next person too:

| You have                                          | Go to                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A question, or trouble setting up your own server | [Discussions → Q&A](https://github.com/atlastodo/atlas/discussions/categories/q-a)       |
| An idea or a wish                                 | [Discussions → Ideas](https://github.com/atlastodo/atlas/discussions/categories/ideas)   |
| A bug you can describe, or a well-defined feature | [an issue](https://github.com/atlastodo/atlas/issues/new/choose)                         |
| A security problem                                | [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md): privately, never in a public issue                        |
| A problem with a server someone else runs         | that server's admin (the app's _Report a problem_ screen reaches them, not this project) |

Before asking, the [self-hosting guide](../docs/self-hosting.md) covers settings, reverse proxies,
backups and upgrades, and [the roadmap](../ROADMAP.md) says what is planned and what is not.

## What to expect

- Issues and discussions are read and triaged about once a week. If nothing happened on your pull
  request after 7 days, comment on it to ping.
- Security reports are acknowledged within 7 days ([SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md#what-happens-next)).
- Only the latest release gets fixes. Please check a bug against it before reporting.
- Releases ship when they are ready, with no fixed schedule.
- Requests that don't fit [the roadmap](../ROADMAP.md) may be declined, with the reason. The
  [design decisions](../docs/decisions) explain the bigger ones.
- There is no paid support or uptime guarantee, including for the test server at
  app.atlastodo.dev.
